suggIntro: Things the app noticed and can do for you. They stay here until you act on them or clear them.
suggTip: Suggestions: things the app can do for you
ruleOfferN: {n} other item looks like "{kw}". A rule gives them the category {cat}, and future ones too. | {n} other items look like "{kw}". A rule gives them the category {cat}, and future ones too.
ruleOffer0: No other items look like "{kw}" yet, but a rule would catch future ones.
roText: You put {name} in {cat}. A rule puts similar items in this category, now and in the future.
roSim: {n} other item contains "{kw}" and will be put in {cat} now: {list} | {n} other items contain "{kw}" and will be put in {cat} now: {list}
roNone: No other items contain "{kw}". The rule will apply to future ones.
needKw: Type the text to match first
cpOfferT: Always count these as card payments?
cpOfferN: {n} other payment to “{desc}” looks the same. A rule counts them all, and future ones, as card payments. | {n} other payments to “{desc}” look the same. A rule counts them all, and future ones, as card payments.
cpOffer0: No other payments look like “{desc}” yet, but a rule would recognise future ones.
cpDone: Rule added. {n} more payment now counts as a card payment. | Rule added. {n} more payments now count as a card payment.
cpDone0: Rule added. Future payments like this are recognised as card payments.
tagRuleDone: Rule created. {n} transaction tagged. | Rule created. {n} transactions tagged.
tagRuleDone0: Rule created. It tags new transactions.
tagRuleText: You tagged {name} with {tags}. A rule does this automatically for similar transactions from now on.
nrToast: If {field} {how} “{k}” → “{name}”. {c} entry renamed. See it in Settings → Display names. | If {field} {how} “{k}” → “{name}”. {c} entries renamed. See it in Settings → Display names.

chip.twinTip: The same refund appears on your card and in your bank a few days apart, so it may be counted twice. Open the entry to count it once.
chip.expLate: The bank has not listed this charge yet. It stays here until the charge appears.
chip.expNote: The app expects this bill based on your past payments. It is not a transaction yet and is not in the totals. Click to open the bill.
chip.upNote: The bank listed this ahead of time, for example a card purchase that will be charged on that date, an instalment or a standing order. It is not in the totals until that day.

why.once: You marked this payment as a bill. It counts once.
why.manual: You told the app that every payment to "{m}" is a bill.
why.irr: {sc}Every payment to "{m}" counts as a bill, even though the timing varies. So far you have made {n} payment, {c} of them in the last 12 months. | {sc}Every payment to "{m}" counts as a bill, even though the timing varies. So far you have made {n} payments, {c} of them in the last 12 months.
why.found: The app found it by itself: you were charged {n} time, {cad}, for a similar amount (about {amt}). | The app found it by itself: you were charged {n} times, {cad}, for a similar amount (about {amt}).
why.fut: Scheduled for {d}. {src} listed it ahead of time{p}, for example a card purchase that will be charged on that date, an instalment or a standing order. It is not in the totals until that day.

w.jarAuto: {amt} came out of {jar}{done}, because {cat} is a category this jar pays for.
w.detachText: It will no longer count as paid from the jar.
w.notJar: {cat} is a category {jar} pays for, but nothing was taken from it for this payment (you detached it, or the jar was empty). It came from your own money.
w.unbillText: The app will stop treating this payment as a bill.
w.twin: This looks like the same {amt} refund counted twice: {w1} on {d1} and {w2} on {d2} ({name}). Count it once.
w.billTileS: The app will expect it again
w.jarTileS: Paid out of one of your jars
w.bmOnceS: A one-off bill that does not repeat. Use it for something that will not come again.
w.bmRuleS: Each payment counts as a bill, even if the timing varies. Irregular ones still show in Bills.
w.bmAuto: Work it out from the payments
w.bmAlreadyS: Payments to this business or person are already bills
w.jaNeed: Enter how much came from the jar
w.jaEmpty: That jar is empty, so nothing can be taken from it
w.jaNothing: Nothing is set aside in this jar for that payment
w.jaHEmpty: The jar holds {have}, so it will be emptied{rest}.
w.jaHRest: (the rest of the payment came from elsewhere)
w.jaHNeed: Enter how much of the payment came from the jar.
w.jeText: Is this jar finished? Marking it as done moves it to Completed jars. It keeps its history and the payment you attached, and stops taking new money.

dv.title: {name} · {n} attachment | {name} · {n} attachments
dv.choose: Choose a file to preview it.
dv.nameOnly: This file was recorded by name only, so there is nothing to preview.
dv.noPreview: This type of file cannot be previewed here.
dv.pdfFail: This PDF could not be shown here.

a.expTip: Download your transactions as a file.
a.focusN: Showing only {n} item | Showing only {n} items
a.focusText: {label}. Everything else is hidden until you clear this.
a.gapPart: ({amt} originally, part of it already explained)
a.gapOut: Your {name} balance dropped by {amt}{part} between {from} and {to}, the times of two syncs. The balance itself is right. What is missing is the transaction, so your spending in reports is too low until you add it.
a.gapIn: Your {name} balance rose by {amt}{part} between {from} and {to}, the times of two syncs. The balance itself is right. What is missing is the transaction, so your income in reports is too low until you add it.
a.cardOut: What you owe on {name} went up by {amt}{part} between {from} and {to}, the times of two syncs. That amount is right. What is missing is the purchase, so your spending in reports is too low until you add it.
a.cardIn: What you owe on {name} went down by {amt}{part} between {from} and {to}, the times of two syncs, and no payment of the card bill was found. Usually the bill was paid from an account that is not connected here, and then nothing is wrong: dismiss it with a note. It can also be a refund the card has not listed yet.
a.gapCauses: Usual causes: a purchase the bank lists with no amount yet (it fills in at a later sync, and this clears by itself), a payment the bank has not posted yet, a fee, or older history that was never imported (try Import history in Settings → Connections).
a.gapBill: This looks like {bill} (about {amt}), expected around {date}. The bank has not listed it yet, so nothing is needed from you. It closes by itself when the transaction appears.
a.gapAddTip: Opens the add form with the amount and date filled in, so you can name it and pick a category.
a.upcatTip: This is an expected bill, not a payment yet. The category you choose also applies to this bill’s next payments.
a.stillTitle: Still to come in this group
a.stillNote: The numbers in this header count only what has already happened. Expected items, such as a bill that has not been charged yet, are shown in the table but are not included until they happen.
